chats.answer:
For a 16-inch MacBook Pro, I'd buy the Anker 140W 4-Port charger (A2697) at the price below. It supports USB Power Delivery 3.1, can supply 140W to the MacBook from a high-power USB-C port when used alone, and costs substantially less than Apple's adapter. If you want a direct replacement for the original charger with no power-sharing considerations, choose Apple's instead.

Best picks

Anker 140W 4-Port Charger (A2697)

$53.99

B&H Photo

Best overall value. Three USB-C ports, one USB-A port and a power display. Connecting other devices reduces the power available to the MacBook.

Apple 140W USB-C Power Adapter

$99.00

Best Buy

Best first-party choice. One dedicated 140W USB-C port; charging cable sold separately.

Insignia 140W USB-C GaN Wall Charger

$44.99

Best Buy

Budget option if you only need a laptop charger. I found less independent testing for this model, so I'd spend the extra $9 on the Anker.

Make sure you actually get fast charging

Use your existing USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable if you have one. It's the straightforward fast-charging connection for 16-inch models from 2021 onward. Newer models can also fast-charge through USB-C with a suitable 240W-rated cable; the 2021 and 2022 models need MagSafe 3 for full fast charging. A 100W USB-C cable will limit power.

For any third-party charger, look for 140W from one port using USB PD 3.1 EPR (28V/5A), not merely 140W summed across several ports. A charger with more than 140W total capacity can be useful if you need to power a phone without sacrificing the MacBook's full allocation. 
The Gadget Masters

I assumed you have a 2021-or-newer model and are shopping in the US. These are advertised prices, not checkout-verified totals, and I haven't independently tested the chargers' heat or sustained output.
